- **"one group at a time, before presenting any group to the user":** this is an ordering of the agent's behavior, so it is observable behavior. The skill could express it in many ways.

It calls `step_of` on the skill's parsed Workflow steps with the phrase "If you can't start subagents, review each group yourself against the prompt, one group at a time". `step_of` panics if no workflow step contains that phrase. That covers the subagents-unavailable condition, self-review, review against the prompt, and one group at a time (a–c). The skill's step 3 contains that sentence, in the same step that points to `references/review-prompt.md`.

The test then asserts that the fallback step's number is strictly less than the number of the step containing "Present each group to the user". That covers the ordering obligation (d). If the fallback moved after presentation, or lost its wording, the test would fail.

The phrase check cannot show that "the prompt" is the review prompt. That prompt is defined and tested under `review_prompt`. The sentence sits in the step that names it, so this is not a separate obligation needing its own test. I found no gap.

The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST supply the review prompt that each group's reviewer follows. The prompt MUST direct the reviewer not to edit files. It MUST direct the reviewer to make mechanical changes itself in the revised text it returns, and to return design questions for the user.
